newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha stable to firm. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha stable to firm. [CORRECTED 12:00 GMT]

text.p: Tokyo Naphtha prices were stable to a tad firmer in quiet afternoon trade on Tuesday after overnight overseas crude markets failed to provide clear market direction.
(Corrects headline and text to show that naphtha prices were not "higher" but "stable to firm". Removes references to crude prices going up.)
Open-spec naphtha for first-half January was quoted at $219.00/$221.00, compared with $218.50/$219.50 in late Monday trading.
Second-half December was assessed around $1.00 higher than the first-half January level, and second-half January was indicated about $1.00 below.
In inter-month naphtha spreads, first-half December/first-half January was discussed at plus $1.75/$2.00, while second-half December/second-half January was talked at plus $1.75/$2.50.

In term price negotiations for Saudi Arabian naphtha cargoes, the premium for Ras Tanura A-180 was set at $6.50 over the Aramco formula for the first six months of 1997, traders said. The new price compares with the current premium of $3.40 for the second half of 1996, they said.
Jubail naphtha premium was hiked by $2.50 to $5.50, the traders said. -- Tokyo Energy Desk, 81-3-3432-8837
